stem: A 41-year-old day laborer presents with about ten weeks of cough and intermittent low-grade fevers, which he attributed to seasonal changes and kept working through because he is paid by the day. He has hypertension that he manages with medication obtained sporadically from a local pharmacy, and admits he often skips doses when money is tight. He denies significant weight loss but his wife says his appetite has clearly dropped. He has never been treated for TB and has no known contact with anyone with drug-resistant TB; he has not traveled outside the area and has no known HIV risk factors. Sputum smear is negative, Xpert MTB/RIF positive, rifampicin not detected. Chest imaging shows a non-cavitary right infiltrate. Exam: BP 148/92, mildly overweight, scattered crackles.

patient.social_history: Lives with wife; paid by the day, so continued working through symptoms; inconsistent access to his regular medication
patient.presenting_complaint: Cough, intermittent low-grade fevers, reduced appetite
patient.exam_findings: BP 148/92, mildly overweight, scattered crackles, non-cavitary right infiltrate on imaging
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: Poorly controlled hypertension and medication non-adherence proposed as the driver of his nonspecific fatigue rather than an infectious process
Seasonal viral illness assumed responsible for the intermittent fevers given the timing
ntep_correct_actions: Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.
Do not order mycobacterial culture as a routine parallel test alongside the initial molecular test; reserve culture for the downstream resistance-testing cascade after a positive molecular result.
Administer first-line anti-TB therapy on a daily dosing schedule throughout both the intensive and continuation phases; do not offer an intermittent (thrice- or twice-weekly) dosing option.

Do not order mycobacterial culture as a routine parallel test alongside the initial molecular test; reserve culture for the downstream resistance-testing cascade after a positive molecular result.
Administer first-line anti-TB therapy on a daily dosing schedule throughout both the intensive and continuation phases; do not offer an intermittent (thrice- or twice-weekly) dosing option.
us_correct_actions: Reserve rapid rifampicin-resistance testing for patients who meet at least one specific risk criterion (prior TB treatment, birth in or residence in a higher-TB-incidence country, contact with a known MDR-TB case, or HIV infection); do not order it routinely for a patient with none of these risk factors.
Send both liquid and solid mycobacterial culture on the initial specimen regardless of the molecular test result, since culture is considered the gold-standard microbiologic test.

Continuation-phase dosing may be switched to thrice-weekly (or twice-weekly if directly observed therapy is difficult), since this patient is HIV-negative and at low relapse risk (non-cavitary, smear-negative disease).
critical_error_conditions: Omitting rifampicin-resistance testing on the assumption this patient's presentation is inherently low-risk for resistant disease
Initiating an intermittent dosing schedule at treatment start rather than daily dosing throughout
expected_divergence_points: Whether rifampicin-resistance testing is ordered universally or only for patients meeting specific US risk criteria
Whether mycobacterial culture is ordered as a mandatory parallel test or reserved for the resistance-detection cascade
Whether daily dosing is used throughout treatment or intermittent dosing is offered for a low-relapse-risk patient
